discovery: Metal-halide perovskite semiconductors for efficient solution-processed photovoltaics
motivation: Miyasaka first used methylammonium lead halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells (2009). Park demonstrated the first stable solid-state perovskite cells, with about 9% efficiency (2012). Snaith showed that the perovskite itself carries charge over long distances and works as a thin-film semiconductor without a mesoporous scaffold (2012–2013). His measurements of diffusion lengths longer than a micron revealed an unusual physical property: a solution-processed, low-temperature material that tolerates defects and has sharp absorption edges, low Urbach energies and high photoluminescence yields close to those of the best crystalline III–V semiconductors. In just over a decade, single-junction efficiencies have passed 26% and perovskite–silicon tandems have passed 33%, and the materials also support LEDs, lasers and detectors. The discovery changed our understanding of how disorder, polarons and defect physics limit semiconductors. It is also starting to change how solar energy is generated.
